findings.description: every problem found, most severe first; an empty array is a valid answer

file.description: path of the file the finding is in, relative to the working directory

line.description: 1-indexed anchor line, or 0 for a file-level finding with no single line

end_line.description: last line of the range, or 0 when the finding is a single line

severity.description: critical breaks correctness or security, major is a real defect, minor is a smaller problem worth fixing

confidence.description: how sure you are the problem is real, 0-100, scored on how far you actually verified it. 40 — it looks wrong from reading, but you did not confirm it. 60 — you confirmed the code says what you claim, but not that the failure follows. 85 — you traced the path from an input the code accepts to the failure. 95 — you traced it and something independent confirms it: a test, a run, or a written rule naming this case. If you did not open the code and follow it through, you are below 60. This measures whether the finding is real and nothing else — how bad it would be and how often it happens are severity's job, not this field's.

body.description: what is wrong and what it causes, with the concrete failure case

fix.description: the smallest change that resolves it, empty when there is no obvious fix

lenses.description: the lenses you carry that raised this finding, using only lens names you were given
